label: Promo C (P-C) deck-code entities the game itself wrote
what: Deck-code (QR) entities for the eight Promo C printings P-C 002-009, read from two real in-game deck QRs. Kept apart from lib/c1_provisional_entities.json (its counts and build are untouched) and from the catalog. lib/encode_qr.py and lib/decode_qr.py read it through lib/check_c1_overlay.py load_promo(), only for ids and entities the catalog lacks (the catalog always wins). Only numbers the game wrote are here: no guesses.
source: from the owner's in-game QR, Nov 18 2026 ('New deck 4'); raw payload AZic/BMAWXQAVxwAV5QAV54AV3YAWD4AWGYAVb4AWCAAWWAAVUYAVq4AWI4AWc4AV04AWboAWMoAV0QAVnIDBQcG
source_2: from the owner's in-game QR, Nov 20 2026 ('New deck 1', which the owner says holds all the Promo C cards available through the Dual Fusion event; it also holds Zoroark ex, Mega Audino ex, Pikachu and Bewear ex, which read as their existing cards); raw payload AZidfhMAXXAAXUgAV4oAV5QAV54AV54AV3YATHIAXWYAWcQAWcQAWc4AWc4AWboAWboARowAXXoAWaYAN0YDBQED
evidence: Re-encoding each deck's 20 cards by these ids gives a payload byte-identical to the scanned one (lib/test_promo_c.py). Which new number belongs to which card comes from slot position (the other Pokemon slots follow the screen order exactly; the one Trainer slot is Genome Converter Y); the bytes alone do not name the card.
left_out: Numbers the Nov 20 code also holds for cards the catalog and engine have no id for, so not entered: Torchic pokemon:23920, Chikorita 23880, Treecko 23910, Mudkip 23930 (promo-badged starters; the engine's P-C list stops at P-C 013), and Bewear ex 22950 (C1 118, exactly the C1 117 + 10 the C1 overlay declined to assume; it belongs to that overlay, not here).
